extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of political philosophy and designers of utopian/state institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and principles for constituting and governing an ideal guardian class within a city-state (education, family structure, reproduction, property, military conduct, and honors). Extracts normative prescriptions and practical arrangements intended for a legislator constructing such a polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal education for suitable women and men
rubrics_metrics.description: The same education which makes a man a good guardian will make a woman a good guardian; for their original nature is the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select women who resemble male guardians in capacity and character and give them the same instruction (music, gymnastic, philosophy) so that natures of like quality have like pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by nature/ability, not sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Those women who have such qualities are to be selected as the companions and colleagues of men who have similar qualities and whom they resemble in capacity and in character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians (male or female) are chosen based on comparative strength or weakness in relevant qualities; selection mirrors the process used for male guardians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women share in music and gymnastic; lighter labours assigned
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the wives of our guardians strip, for their virtue will be their robe, and let them share in the toils of war and the defence of their country; only in the distribution of labours the lighter are to be assigned to the women, who are the weaker natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women partake in physical training and music alongside men; where physical difference mandates, assign lighter tasks but preserve equality of duties in other respects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of wives and children (no private families)
rubrics_metrics.description: The wives of our guardians are to be common, and their children are to be common, and no parent is to know his own child, nor any child his parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This communal arrangement is presented as a major law of the state; it is asserted to increase unity and reduce private rivalries tied to 'mine' and 'not mine.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of pleasures and pains as highest good
rubrics_metrics.description: There is unity where there is community of pleasures and pains—where all the citizens are glad or grieved on the same occasions of joy and sorrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation should seek to create common interests and shared feelings among citizens (e.g., through community of families/property) as the chief aim of the legislator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians hold no private property; receive subsistence only
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardians were not to have houses or lands or any other property; their pay was to be their food, which they were to receive from the other citizens, and they were to have no private expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abolish private possessions for the guardian class to remove causes of suits, complaints, and divisions; their maintenance is public and limited to essentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians live communally (houses, meals, exercises)
rubrics_metrics.description: They must live in common houses and meet at common meals. None of them will have anything specially his or her own; they will be together, and will be brought up together, and will associate at gymnastic exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common living arrangements foster unity and shared habits; communal upbringing integrates duties and loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled breeding: breed the best with the best
rubrics_metrics.description: The best of either sex should be united with the best as often, and the inferior with the inferior, as seldom as possible; and that they should rear the offspring of the one sort of union, but not of the other, if the flock is to be maintained in first-rate condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers must regulate unions to preserve the quality of the guardian breed; this includes selective pairing and preventing inferior offspring from being reared publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers may employ lawful falsehoods for the state's good
rubrics_metrics.description: Our rulers will find a considerable dose of falsehood and deceit necessary for the good of their subjects: we were saying that the use of all these things regarded as medicines might be of advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Noble lies’ or paternal deceptions are defended as instruments (like medicines) to maintain order and implement sensitive measures (e.g., controlled breeding) that must remain secret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate marriages and births via festivals and lotteries
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint certain festivals at which we will bring together the brides and bridegrooms... The number of weddings is a matter which must be left to the discretion of the rulers... We shall have to invent some ingenious kind of lots which the less worthy may draw on each occasion... and then they will accuse their own ill-luck and not the rulers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ceremonials, sacrificial observances, and staged randomness to disguise state regulation of pairings and to maintain consent and social cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population management: rulers regulate number of weddings
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of weddings is a matter which must be left to the discretion of the rulers, whose aim will be to preserve the average of population... consider effects of wars and diseases... to prevent the State from becoming either too large or too small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislators must monitor and adjust births in light of demographic pressures, wars, and disease to maintain a stable, optimal population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret handling/disposal of inferior or deformed offspring
rubrics_metrics.description: The offspring of the inferior, or of the better when they chance to be deformed, will be put away in some mysterious, unknown place, as they should be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers must arrange for removal or secrecy concerning certain births to preserve the guardian class; secrecy prevents unrest and maintains morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children reared by appointed nurses; mothers relieved of domestic burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper officers... will deposit them with certain nurses who dwell in a separate quarter; care will also be taken that the process of suckling shall not be protracted too long; and the mothers will have no getting up at night or other trouble, but will hand over all this sort of thing to the nurses and attendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional, state-run nurture assures uniform upbringing, spares guardian mothers from household burdens, and furthers the communal ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime-of-life reproductive age windows (women 20–40, men 25–55)
rubrics_metrics.description: A woman... at twenty years of age may begin to bear children to the State, and continue to bear them until forty; a man may begin at five-and-twenty... and continue to beget children until he be fifty-five.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set explicit age ranges for sanctioned reproduction; unions outside those ranges are pronounced unholy and their offspring are not to be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioned conceptions and illegitimacy rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any one above or below the prescribed ages who takes part in the public hymeneals shall be said to have done an unholy and unrighteous thing; the child of which he is the father... will have been conceived under auspices very unlike the sacrifices and prayers... and the offspring of such an union cannot be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers criminalize or delegitimize conceptions outside sanctioned rites/ages and take steps to prevent such offspring from entering the guardianship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymize parentage; artificial kinship via dating scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Dating from the day of the hymeneal, the bridegroom... will call all the male children who are born in the seventh and tenth month afterwards his sons... All who were begotten at the time when their fathers and mothers came together will be called their brothers and sisters...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use calendrical naming and institutional conventions to erase biological parentage and create civic family bonds; forbid intermarriage among those so designated except by lottery/oracular exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception mechanism: lotteries and Pythian oracle sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: This, however, is not to be understood as an absolute prohibition of the marriage of brothers and sisters; if the lot favours them, and they receive the sanction of the Pythian oracle, the law will allow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide controlled, exceptional pathways (random lot + oracle) to permit rare deviations while maintaining the public legitimacy of pairings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must both obey laws and command with authority
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be willingness to obey in the one and the power of command in the other; the guardians must themselves obey the laws, and they must also imitate the spirit of them in any details which are entrusted to their care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians should model law-abiding behavior and possess legitimate authority; rulers select and train them accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children must be exposed to war-training while being protected
rubrics_metrics.description: Make our children spectators of war; but we must also contrive that they shall be secured against danger... mount them on horses in their earliest youth... so that they will get an excellent view of what is hereafter to be their own business; and if there is danger they have only to follow their elder leaders and escape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early, supervised military exposure and skill training (including horsemanship) prepare youths for service while minimizing mortal risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for cowardice and rewards for valor
rubrics_metrics.description: The soldier who leaves his rank or throws away his arms, or is guilty of any other act of cowardice, should be degraded into the rank of a husbandman or artisan... the hero who has distinguished himself... shall receive honour in the army from his youthful comrades; every one of them in succession shall crown him... right hand of fellowship... let no one whom he has a mind to kiss refuse to be kissed by him while the expedition lasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use demotion/punishment to deter cowardice and public honors (crowns, fellowship, symbolic kisses, precedence, more wives/children) to incentivize bravery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public honors and sacred burial for the gloriously brave
rubrics_metrics.description: When a man dies gloriously in war shall we not say, in the first place, that he is of the golden race?... We must learn of the god how we are to order the sepulture of divine and heroic personages... and in ages to come we will reverence them and kneel before their sepulchres as at the graves of heroes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutionalize special funerary rites and ongoing veneration for exemplary warriors to promote civic ideals and remembrance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of enemies and rules of warfare among Hellenes
rubrics_metrics.description: No Hellene should be owned by them as a slave... we must abstain from spoiling the dead or hindering their burial... Neither shall we offer up arms at the temples of the gods, least of all the arms of Hellenes... both devastation of lands and the burning of houses should be forbidden; I would take the annual produce and no more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate 'discord' (internal Hellenic strife) from foreign war: among co-nationals prohibit enslavement, looting of corpses, burning houses, and excessive devastation; prefer limited exactions (annual produce) and humane treatment to preserve shared bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish war from discord; temper intra-national conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a difference in the names ‘discord’ and ‘war’... when Hellenes fight with one another we shall say that Hellas is then in a state of disorder and discord... such enmity is to be called discord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat internal conflicts as correctable disputes among friends; aim for reconciliation and limited penalties rather than total destruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communal arrangements reduce petty evils and encourage blessed life
rubrics_metrics.description: From all these evils they will be delivered, and their life will be blessed as the life of Olympic victors and yet more blessed... the many evils of so many kinds which people suffer in this way are mean enough and obvious enough, and not worth speaking of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present communal property, families, and public maintenance as means to eliminate petty jealousies, economic burdens, and corruptions associated with private household competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation should aim for greatest good of the whole State
rubrics_metrics.description: We were fashioning the State with a view to the greatest happiness, not of any particular class, but of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All institutional choices (family law, education, property, military practice) should be justified by their contribution to the common good rather than sectional advantage.
